#: SCARLIX OS v19.1.15 — Pi-Bolt coding agent configuration (TEMPLATE — no real secrets)
#_description: Pi-Bolt (https://github.com/opensec-git/Pi-Bolt) is a fork of Pi compiled AOT to native code. It uses Pi's config directory (~/.pi/agent) and OpenAI-compatible providers. This template preserves the functional intent of the previous OpenCode config: (1) uses existing LiteLLM gateway, (2) accesses ScarliHQ MCP, (3) has plan + build agents, (4) does not bypass network/security architecture.
#_install: Pi-Bolt is installed as non-root user via: curl -fsSL https://pi-bolt.opensec.in/install.sh | sh (see install.sh Phase 5). The installer places Pi-Bolt under ~/.pi-bolt and links ~/.local/bin/pi-bolt. This config is a TEMPLATE — the actual runtime config is generated at ~/.pi/agent/ by the install script + user setup.
#_security: LITELLM_MASTER_KEY is read from /etc/scarlix/.env (root:root 600) at runtime — NEVER hardcode a real key in this file. The ${LITELLM_MASTER_KEY} pattern matches agents/hermes/config.yaml.
#_model_note: scarlix-default is the LiteLLM model alias (not a backend model ID). LiteLLM routes it to SGLang (primary) -> Ollama -> BeeLlama fallback. See ai/litellm/config.yaml.

openai.#_baseURL_note: LiteLLM gateway binds to 127.0.0.1:4001 (host port) -> container :4000. Pi-Bolt runs on the host (non-root user), so localhost is correct. The old OpenCode used 100.64.0.1:4000 (Headscale VPN IP) — Pi-Bolt uses localhost per the security principle that inference endpoints are localhost-only.
openai.#_apiKey_note: Env var substitution — Pi-Bolt/Pi reads this from the environment. The actual key is in ~/.config/scarlix/agent.env (generated by install.sh from /etc/scarlix/.env, root:root 600). Install.sh exports it to the user's shell profile via a safe mechanism (NOT committed).

scarlihq.#_url_note: ScarliHQ MCP endpoint (JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP). Binds to 127.0.0.1:8090 (dashboard + MCP on same port). The old OpenCode used :8091 — but ScarliHQ serves both REST/WS and MCP on :8090 (see scarlihq/internal/mcp/server.go).
scarlihq.#_auth_note: ScarliHQ MCP requires Bearer token auth (SCARLIHQ_TOKEN from env). Pi-Bolt must send Authorization header.

#_workflow: Pi-Bolt preserves the functional distinction: PLAN mode (read-only, propose changes) -> BUILD mode (edit, test, git diff). Destructive git actions require human approval (per ScaRgeN master guide section 42, section 17).
#_extensions: Minimal required only: core Pi-Bolt + opensec-pi-subagents (if multi-agent workflows needed). Do NOT install every available extension — treat extensions as executable code (section 20).
#_rollback: The previous OpenCode config is preserved at agents/opencode/config.json.DEPRECATED for rollback. If Pi-Bolt fails acceptance, restore via: git revert <migration-commit>.
#_references: Pi-Bolt repo: https://github.com/opensec-git/Pi-Bolt | Pi packages: https://pi.dev/packages | Migration guide: docs/SCARLIX_AGENT_MIGRATION_OpenCode_to_PiBolt.md
